first.rationale: Current situation shows simultaneous drops in activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ). Memory 31 established that signup simplification improved SMB activation durably, and memory 86 confirmed that shortening onboarding lifted early adoption. These directly address the observed metrics decline. I am verifying memory 31 and 73 to confirm: (1) whether the original signup simplification effect holds under current cohorts, and (2) whether promotional pricing remains viable given competitive pressure or if it risks margin erosion that undermines long-term qualified revenue. The primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not short-term acquisition volume. Simplify_onboarding addresses the measured activation/completion decline with a proven lever, while a standard_experiment scope allows iteration if results are weaker than archived performance. This preserves the option to pivot toward promotional_pricing if onboarding simplification shows diminished returns, and avoids the referral/enterprise paths which address different bottlenecks not yet validated as primary constraints.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms memory_31 is reliable: signup simplification delivered +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB with only -1% retention drag. Memory_73 reveals critical risk: promotional pricing acquired customers at -12% 30-day retention, failing the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Current metrics show activation down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ—exactly the failure modes that simplification addressed in exp_31. Competitor pricing pressure argues for defensible product-driven growth, not margin-eroding discounts. Simplify_onboarding is the only tested lever that improves both the measured metrics (activation, onboarding completion) and sustains retention. Standard_experiment scale allows measurement of whether the +9% activation lift replicates under current conditions while preserving optionality to escalate or iterate. This avoids the retention risk of promotional_pricing and focuses on the bottleneck demonstrated by current data.
